messages:
support_erin: FYI - ACME (customer) opened a P1 ticket: hosted-api streaming endpoints returning 502/504 for ~30% of requests since 09:12 UTC. They say it started after increasing embed batch sizes. Ticket: #ACME-12345. Repro CURL below.

support_erin: curl -v -X POST "https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/streaming/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME_TOKEN>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --http2 -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","batch_size":64,"inputs":["long doc..."]}'

support_erin: Response intermittently returns HTTP/2 502 with body: \"Upstream connection closed\" and response header x-request-id: acme-req-2026-09

customer_ops_olivia: Pasted a sample trace id from ACME: acme-req-2026-09. Here are the raw upstream snippets they pasted: 

customer_ops_olivia: [upstream] ERROR: "upstream prematurely closed connection" service=ingress-gw pod=ingress-7c9f

eng-sre_jake: Thanks @support_erin @customer_ops_olivia. Can someone grab the full x-request-id and the envoy/access logs for the timeframe 09:10-09:40 UTC? Also share the client behavior (long-lived streams, chunked uploads?).

support_erin: Client uses long-lived streaming websockets -> server-side streaming chunked responses. They sent back-to-back embed batches to same session for ~6min.

observability-bot: alert: edge.gateway.5xx_rate spike (09:11-09:28 UTC) - 502s up 28% vs baseline. Dashboard: https://obs.redwood.ai/d/edge/502-spike?from=1699999800&to=1699999800

runtime_chen: Early guess: h2 keepalive pool exhaustion / max_concurrent_streams limit on Envoy + upstream auth/billing proxy occasionally rejecting new streams -> RST/502 when stream limit hit. Similar to past long-stream embeds issues. Can we check envoy per-connection stream counts and upstream auth cache metrics (miss vs hit)?

product_sam: ACME did note they bumped batch_size to 64 and kept sessions open to reduce latency. They did this exactly around 09:10 UTC.

eng-sre_jake: Repro steps requested from me: 1) Reproduce with curl using --http2 and repeated streams. 2) Run tcpdump on ingress to look for RSTs. 3) Query Envoy metrics: cluster.<auth>.upstream_rq_.* and http2.conn.<id>.active_streams.

eng-sre_jake: Quick check in prod logs for acme-req-2026-09: 

eng-sre_jake: [ingress] 2026-03-18T09:15:22Z "POST /v1/streaming/generate" 502 prox_upstream_reset reason=UPSTREAM_REMOTE_RESET x-request-id=acme-req-2026-09 upstream_host=10.12.3.45:8443

runtime_chen: That upstream_host (10.12.3.45) is authz-proxy-2 in eu-west-1. Authz logs show brief 429 spikes and occasional 503s at 09:12-09:16 (likely internal rate cap during high connection churn). If authz returns non-200, Envoy will surface as 502.

support_erin: Customer confirms they saw increased latency first, then 502 bursts. They rolled back batch_size to 16 and errors dropped to <1% within 6 minutes. :thumbsup:

eng-sre_jake: Good confirmation that it's load profile change. Short-term mitigation: ask customer to keep batch_size <= 16 OR reduce concurrent open sessions. Also temporary fix on our side: increase authz-proxy token cache size and bump Envoy max_concurrent_streams per connection.

runtime_chen: Proposed config patch: set envoy_http2_max_concurrent_streams = 200 (was 100) and tune h2 connection window. Will open a small change with canary to egde-ingress next 30m. (non-invasive, short window).

deploy-bot: deploy: rollout edge-ingress/ingress-gw v2.14.7 -> v2.14.8 (canary 1/4) by runtime_chen at 09:50 UTC

eng-sre_jake: Also adding a rate-limiter exception for ACME to authz (to reduce auth 429s until we stabilize). We should monitor for N+ errors; I'll add a dashboard panel for auth upstream 5xx/429.

support_erin: Noted. ACME accepted temporary workaround and reduced batch_size. They want a permanent recommendation in docs for embedding long-lived streams (we should add a best-practice).

product_sam: Action item: product/docs to add guidance: recommend batch_size, prefer multiple short sessions vs single long session, client-side retry/backoff for 502s. I'll own a doc PR.

customer_ops_olivia: Customer is on standby to test the canary patch. They will try a controlled increase to batch_size=32 tomorrow AM and report.

eng-sre_jake: Post-mortem notes draft: cause=client increased batch/concurrency leading to authz-proxy rate/miss spikes -> envoys hit stream/concurrency boundary -> upstream resets surfaced as 502/504s. Mitigations: short-term customer rollback, increase auth cache + Envoy stream limits; long-term: autoscale authz or add graceful queuing and clearer 429->retry guidance.

support_erin: Thanks team. I'll update ticket #ACME-12345 with workaround and link to canary. Closing once ACME verifies tomorrow.

runtime_chen: Adding follow-up: we'll test that the canary doesn't regress memory footprint before full roll.

support_erin: Closing note: customer verified reduced errors after rollback. Will re-open if spike returns. :white_check_mark:
